candidates.decision_summary: Task1 is high-quality. The paper is observational and the focal claim concerns whether SMD election rules make plurality winners closer to the median voter; the authorized dataset is an election-observation archive with repeated observations by country, pldist1 is a positive nonmissing Manifesto-method plurality-winner distance variable, smd contains pr/smd plus two missing values, and year spans 1945-2003. The candidate uses the authorized DTA, pldist1, the SMD-versus-PR contrast, the relevant full sample after excluding only non-smd/pr and focal missing/nonpositive values, and no invented controls. The Gamma log-link model is an explicit model-family deviation from the anchor's linear regression or mean-comparison reference, but it is justified by the positive right-skewed outcome and still directly tests whether expected distance is lower under SMD via a negative log coefficient or ratio below 1; guardrails G1 and G14 apply, and no M1-M6 or Task1 low-quality rule is triggered. The code implements the declared model and sample flow, verifies required columns, reports focal coefficient, HC1 uncertainty, confidence interval, exponentiated ratio, group summaries, final n, and applies the fixed support/opposite/inconclusive rule. Repeated country observations are present, but the anchor does not require clustered inference and there is no clear evidence under Rule 1.6 that HC1 robust covariance makes the focal inference unreliable for this candidate. Prior shared-memory paths used OLS with decade fixed effects and median quantile regression, so this Gamma GLM is not a semantic duplicate.
